claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can initially exist as a homogeneous high-temperature BCC phase.
Al atoms induce local lattice distortions in the BCC matrix.
Al-induced lattice distortions reduce the local mixing free energy in specific regions of the BCC matrix.
Regions with reduced local mixing free energy are thermodynamically unstable relative to the high-temperature BCC matrix.
Al-rich compositional fluctuations act as nucleation sites for secondary phases during cooling.
The extent of phase transformation is governed by competition between local thermodynamic instability and kinetic barriers to atomic diffusion.
Changing the cooling rate modulates atomic mobility and thereby permits or suppresses local chemical inhomogeneity.
Local Al-rich clusters or chemical short-range order induce lattice strain and lower the local free-energy barrier for phase transformation.
Slow cooling provides sufficient atomic mobility for Al segregation and cluster formation.
Al-rich clusters promote nucleation of B2 or sigma secondary phases.
Rapid quenching suppresses atomic diffusion and retains a metastable BCC structure.
Slowly cooled samples will have a higher secondary-phase volume fraction than rapidly quenched samples.
Secondary phases in slowly cooled samples will be localized near regions of elevated Al concentration.
The transformation onset temperature will differ between slowly cooled and rapidly quenched samples.
Phase fraction and transformation kinetics will correlate with the extent of local Al segregation.
The proposed mechanism applies only under impurity-controlled conditions and in a temperature regime where BCC is metastable.
Oxidation or extreme processing rates could alter the proposed transformation behavior.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says that reducing local mixing free energy makes a region thermodynamically unstable, whereas the mediator and mechanism shift to lowering a transformation barrier. A lower state free energy and a lower kinetic barrier are distinct effects, and the text does not reconcile why reduced mixing free energy destabilizes rather than stabilizes the Al-rich region.
